01

Positioning

Lead with the physical modeling problem, the candidate model, and the decision it supports.

Working company description / Current

Carbon finds and develops fast physics models for specific engineering problems, combining competitive research with independent evaluation.

High-fidelity simulation is accurate, yet slow runtimes limit how many designs or actions a team can test. Carbon connects scoped physical problems with competitive model discovery, isolated reconstruction, and hidden-exam evaluation to find repeatable methods that stay accurate on hard physics, hold up near limits, and transfer to unfamiliar systems.

The engineering & platform thesis

Predict what happens. Know when to trust it. Choose the next action.

Fast predictions only create engineering value when their failure boundaries are known. Carbon turns physical predictions into decisions engineers can trust across design and control.

Primary focus: Model discovery and custom physics AI development.
Platform direction: Physical intelligence (State → Predict → Judge → Decide → Act → Verify → Learn).
Signature: Prove the work.

Messaging priority. Lead commercial and first-touch communication with fast physics models, competitive discovery, and custom model development alongside existing CAD/CAE workflows. Frame Physical Intelligence and closed-loop decision/control models clearly as the broader platform direction rather than claiming every layer is shipped today.
02

Method, loop & current scope

Separate model construction, blind testing, and decision use. State the delivery stage alongside every claim.

01 / Define the job

Lock the physics spec.

Define the physical system, required outputs, operating conditions, reference solver or measurements, and acceptance criteria. Builders see the problem specification, never the protected exam cases.

02 / Discover & rebuild

Compete on methods.

Researchers and autonomous agents explore widely using public challenge kits via Miner Control Center and Miner MCP, submitting reproducible construction recipes that isolated workers rebuild in pinned environments.

03 / Judge, verify & learn

Test blind near limits.

Hidden exams check mandatory physics gates, >500x speed gates, near-limit behavior, design transfer, and calibrated self-trust. Verified outcomes map where a method works and where it fails.

04

Typography

Use the supplied PP Neue Montreal files. Keep technical labels subordinate to the message.

Primary / PP Neue Montreal
Fast physics,
tested blind.
RegularSemiboldExtrabold

Use Semibold for headlines, Regular for interface copy and Text Book for longer reading. Reserve Extrabold for short emphasis. Use −2% to −4% tracking on large headlines and normal tracking for body copy.

Technical / monospace
BENCHMARK / MOTOR 1.8 MAINNET
SPEED GATE / >500X VS REFERENCE SOLVER
TRUST LAYER / SELF-TRUST ACTIVE
VISUAL / ILLUSTRATIVE EXAMPLE

Use monospace for run IDs, units, axes and evidence labels. Neue Montreal Mono remains the intended technical family; this board uses a system monospace fallback because the supplied set contains proportional fonts.

The wordmark is vector artwork. Hairline weights belong in large display experiments, outside small text and social-image body copy. Do not export raw .otf or .woff2 font binaries as loose files in the public repository.

Layout

  • Use generous margins, a strong headline and one supporting idea. Align the visible top of the headline with the full wordmark.
  • Use an underline only when it helps hierarchy. End it at the final headline line’s right edge. Leave unused corners empty.
  • Centre comparison panels within the space below the subheading. Recompose 1:1 and 16:9 layouts; preserve type size.

Images & motion

  • Use hardware-forward, high-contrast studio visuals (electric motor stators/rotors, CNC-machined liquid-cooling cold plates, structural brackets) and crisp vector geometry in monochrome with small Signal Vermilion accents. Keep texture out of reading areas.
  • Do not use crypto coin renders, neon cyberpunk palettes, glowing AI brains, or generic stock montages.
  • Require 4-part separation in system diagrams: 1. Problem Spec & Reference Solver, 2. Competitive Model Discovery, 3. Isolated Rebuild & Hidden Exam, and 4. Verified Decision / Customer Use.
  • Give measured plots their scope, units, and source. Stamp non-measured renders or mock UI cards as Illustrative visual or Illustrative example; do not imply scientific proof through decoration.
07

Voice & sample copy

Speak with direct technical and commercial clarity. Match every statement to supported evidence.

Engineering & commercial

High-fidelity solvers can take hours per run. Carbon finds and develops custom fast physics models around your reference solver, tested blind on cases the builders never saw.

Discovery & hidden exams

Most AI models are graded by the teams that built them. On Carbon, researchers submit reproducible recipes, isolated workers rebuild them, and hidden near-limit exams decide what holds up.

Platform direction

Prediction tells you what might happen; decisions create the value. Carbon is building from fast physics predictors toward calibrated trust and verified engineering choices.

Account voices & editorial bans. Carbon company voice: direct, technical, objective. Nick Fitzpatrick: commercial and buyer-focused on LinkedIn and X. Ryan Bequette: grounded in aerospace verification and subnet engineering on X and technical deep dives. Editorial bans: zero em dashes (use periods, commas, colons, or parentheses), no AI hype words, no rhetorical-question openers, no dramatic one-word fragments, no habitual three-part cadences, and no unrequested emojis or hashtags.
08

Claims, disclosure, ownership & licensing

Match every public statement to its verified technical, scientific, or commercial record.

Audience & network framing

Bittensor is public; lead buyers with physics.

Carbon's discovery engine on Bittensor (Subnet 116) is live and public; the pre-reveal restriction from v2 is retired. With commercial engineering buyers, lead with the physical modeling bottleneck, CAE workflow fit, and tested operating limits, treating Subnet 116 as the research engine under the hood and keeping token mechanics out of customer openings.

With miners, researchers, and network participants, explain challenge rules, recipe reconstruction, and emission decay/burn mechanics clearly. Never publish miner income forecasts or promise token returns, and keep Carbon Physics, Inc. corporate revenue distinct from token economics.

Evidence & claim boundaries

Publish the supported claim.

Separate external literature speedups (such as 1,000x neural operator papers) from Carbon's own challenge gates (>500x speed pass mark) and scoped mainnet results (such as Motor 1.8's 0.11% full-waveform error, 0.03% mean torque error, and learned-model error reductions within that motor topology). Do not imply signed commercial customers, paid pilots, recurring revenue, or deployed control loops without approved records.

Use "Passed Physics Gates" or "Independently Evaluated" rather than bare "Qualified" labels that imply formal industrial certification. Never expose hidden exam cases, future seeds, unreleased audit logs, or private customer CAD.
